titulo: Gerund and participle: Gerund periphrases and uses Spanish avoids

aula.objetivo: Form and use the gerund (regular and irregular, with attached pronouns, in phrases like «llevar», «seguir» and «ir» + gerund, and without the English "-ing" uses Spanish doesn't accept) and the participle (irregular forms, agreement as an adjective, «estar», «tener», «llevar» and «dejar» + participle, absolute constructions).

sessao.titulo: Gerund periphrases and uses Spanish avoids

itens.pt: llevar + time + gerund (to have been …-ing for)
to keep on …-ing, to still be …-ing
to keep on …-ing, to still be …-ing

blocos.titulo: Llevo dos años estudiando, sigo trabajando
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: some verb phrases (conjugated verb + gerund) are very common and precise. STEP 2: «llevar» + time + gerund says how long something has been going on — the Spanish for English "I've been studying for two years": «Llevo dos años estudiando español», «Lleva una hora esperando» (She's been waiting for an hour). STEP 3: «seguir» or «continuar» + gerund says something is still going on — English "still" or "keep -ing": «Sigo trabajando en el mismo sitio» (I still work in the same place), «Continúa lloviendo» (It keeps raining). STEP 4: «ir» + gerund says something is gradually progressing: «Voy mejorando» (I'm getting better and better), «La situación va empeorando». Don't confuse it with «ir a» + infinitive (future plans). STEP 5: «andar» + gerund suggests going around doing something, a repeated, often informal activity: «Anda buscando trabajo» (He's going around looking for work). STEP 6: «venir» + gerund is something that has been going on for a while and continues: «Vengo diciéndolo hace tiempo» (I've been saying it for ages). STEP 7: Spanish doesn't accept the gerund as an adjective or for future plans. "A box containing books" is «una caja que contiene libros». "I'm leaving tomorrow" is «Me voy mañana» or «Salgo mañana» — the English present continuous for arrangements doesn't work with «estar» + gerund. STEP 8: English "on arriving", "when leaving" is «al» + infinitive: «Al llegar, llámame» (When you arrive, call me). And actions in sequence are joined with «y» or with finite verbs: «Entró y se sentó».
blocos.comparacao: English "I've been studying for two years" = «Llevo dos años estudiando», "I'm still living with my parents" = «Sigo viviendo con mis padres». But English "I'm leaving tomorrow" (a plan) is «Me voy mañana», never «estoy yéndome mañana», and "a box containing" is «una caja que contiene».

exemplos.pt: I've been learning Spanish for three years.

tabela.sentido: an action going on from before
on doing, when doing (instead of the gerund)

erros.errado: Voy a estar enviándole el informe mañana.
erros.motivo: English "I'll be sending you the report" can't be copied with «estar» + gerund; Spanish uses the simple future.
The gerund can't work as an adjective (no "a box containing").
For "when you arrive" / "on arriving", use «al» + infinitive.

erros.errado: Llevo dos años que estudio español.
erros.motivo: After «llevar» + time comes the gerund, with no «que».

blocos.enunciado: Talk about yourself out loud with five verb phrases: «Llevo… años…», «Sigo…», «Voy…», «Ando…», «Vengo…». Then give two instructions with «al» + infinitive: «Al llegar,…», «Al salir,…».
Say the gerund of «pedir», «seguir», «dormir», «oír» and «construir». Then say two sentences with a gerund of manner.
